title: Keep one failing CI plug-in from silencing the rest

blocks.text: This practice continues the previous one: `BuildEvents.publish` already walks the plug-ins safely when one of them unsubscribes itself, and now hands each build to each plug-in through `deliver(listener, buildId)`.

Plug-ins are written by other teams. Last night the artifact-cleaner plug-in threw on every build because an agent's disk was full. Every plug-in registered after it stopped hearing about builds, and the code that calls `publish` at the end of a build marked green builds as failed. Nobody running the server could tell which plug-in was at fault.

`BuildEvents` now takes an `onPluginFailure` handler in its constructor. Finish `deliver(listener, buildId)` in `src/main/java/practice/BuildEvents.java` so that a plug-in that throws costs no other plug-in its build, never makes `publish` fail, and is reported to that handler with the build id and the exception it threw. About five lines in total.

cases.says: with no plug-in failing, every plug-in hears every build and nothing is reported
the plug-ins after one that throws still hear the build, and publish returns normally
every failure reaches the failure handler with the build id and the plug-in's own exception, in order
a failure in the last plug-in is reported and does not make publish throw

origin.section: One Listener's Exception Skips the Listeners After It and Reaches the Publisher

concepts: A listener that throws inside a plain loop ends the dispatch for every listener after it, and the exception reaches the publisher's caller.
The subject catches around each listener call and reports the failure where someone sees it, so the other listeners still run and the publisher returns normally.
